newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to offer Union Bank shares to public.
newsitem.headline: Israel to offer Union Bank shares to public.

text.p: The government company charged with selling Israel's state-owned banks said on Thursday it plans an offering of the government's shares in Union Bank in 1997 after a deal to sell its stake to the bank's majority shareholder fell through.

"The Eliahu group didn't come to an agreement with the bank workers so now the government's shares will be offered to the public later in the year, perhaps in August," Meir Jacobsen, managing director of MI Holdings, told Reuters.

Jacobsen said MI Holdings had been trying to sell the government's 23 percent stake in Union Bank to an investment group headed by Israeli businessman Shlomo Eliahu, which now owns 60 percent of the bank.
The Eliahu group decided not to purchase the government's stake after failing to reach an arrangement on a share allocation plan with Union Bank employees, Israel's Globes business daily said.
Jacobsen said MI Holdings would offer 10 percent of the government's shares to bank employees.
Union Bank is Israel's sixth largest bank with $3 billion in assets. Israel's Bank Leumi, which once controlled Union, still holds 16.8 percent.
Union was one of the banks in which the government acquired shares as part of a bailout of bank shareholders after the 1983 stock market crash.
